en.question_text: Which river is popularly known as the lifeline of Madhya Pradesh?

hi.question_text: मध्य प्रदेश की जीवन-रेखा कही जाने वाली नदी कौन-सी है?

explanation.correct_reasoning: The Narmada rises from the Amarkantak plateau and drains the largest part of Madhya Pradesh, which is why it is described as the state's lifeline.

option_explanations.text: The Tapti flows mainly through the southern districts and does not drain the central plateau.
Correct. The Narmada is the principal west-flowing river of Madhya Pradesh.
The Chambal forms part of the northern boundary and drains only the northern districts.
The Betwa is a Yamuna tributary flowing through the north-eastern districts.

revision_takeaways: Narmada is west-flowing; Chambal and Betwa belong to the Ganga basin.
Narmada is the longest west-flowing river of peninsular India.

source_reference.note: Synthetic demonstration content; no source document exists.

en.question_text: Dhupgarh, the highest peak of Madhya Pradesh, is located at which place?

hi.question_text: मध्य प्रदेश की सर्वोच्च चोटी धूपगढ़ किस स्थान पर स्थित है?

explanation.correct_reasoning: Dhupgarh (about 1,352 m) stands in the Satpura range at Pachmarhi and is the highest point in Madhya Pradesh.
revision_takeaways: Pachmarhi is in the Satpura range and is also a biosphere reserve.

en.question_text: Which animal is the state animal of Madhya Pradesh?

hi.question_text: मध्य प्रदेश का राज्य पशु कौन-सा है?

explanation.correct_reasoning: The hard-ground barasingha is the state animal of Madhya Pradesh; the tiger is the national animal.
revision_takeaways: Do not confuse the state animal (barasingha) with the national animal (tiger).

en.question_text: The Bhimbetka rock shelters are located in which district of Madhya Pradesh?

hi.question_text: मध्य प्रदेश में प्रमुख जलाशय बनाने वाली तवा नदी किस नदी की सहायक नदी है?

explanation.correct_reasoning: The Tawa is a left-bank tributary of the Narmada and the Tawa reservoir supplies water to parts of the Narmadapuram region.
key_concepts: Narmada tributaries: Tawa, Barna, Hiran, Bichhiya
revision_takeaways: Left-bank tributaries of the Narmada include Tawa, Barna and Hiran.
